visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Ten questions across the season: Marco reads five, and five more are on the cards. Answer along, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Harbour has an enterprise value of €1.5bn and pays a €100m cash dividend. What happens to its enterprise value?
questions.explain: Equity value falls by €100m and net debt rises by €100m. The business hasn't changed, so enterprise value stays the same.

questions.q: Free cash flow is 100 next year, growing at 2% forever, with a 10% discount rate. What's it worth today?
questions.explain: Cash flow over the discount rate minus growth: 100 ÷ 8% = 1,250. Dividing by 10% gives 1,000 and leaves out the growth.
questions.explain_at: Cash flow over the discount rate minus growth

questions.q: A fund turns 300 of equity into 900 in five years. Roughly what is the IRR?
questions.explain: Tripling in five years compounds at about 25% a year. 60% is simple interest, and 15% only doubles the money.
questions.explain_at: Tripling in five years is about twenty-five percent a year

questions.q: Why is Ass.El.'s €2.5m enterprise value below its €4m equity value?

options.text: It has more debt than cash
The figures are the wrong way round

questions.explain: Ass.El. had €1.5m of net cash at the end of September. Enterprise value is equity value minus net cash: 4 − 1.5 = 2.5.

questions.q: Ass.El.'s enterprise value is €2.5m. What's the multiple on its 2025 EBITDA of about €200k?
questions.explain: €2.5m ÷ €200k = 12.5x. The 4.2x is on the €600k forecast for 2026, so always ask which EBITDA the multiple uses.

questions.q: Northgate has earnings of €100m and 100m shares at €20. It issues €600m of new shares to buy a company earning €50m. What happens to earnings per share?
questions.explain: 30m new shares, but €50m of earnings arrives with them: 150 ÷ 130 is about €1.15. Northgate trades at 20x and buys at 12x.
questions.explain_at: One hundred and fifty over one hundred and thirty

questions.q: A business is worth 400, with 300 of senior loans and 200 of bonds. What do the bonds get, and who is the fulcrum?
questions.explain: The seniors take their 300 first, leaving 100 for the bonds. Debt is a queue, and the fulcrum is where the value runs out.
questions.explain_at: the bonds are where the value runs out

questions.q: An interviewer asks whether Bayer's purchase of Monsanto was a good deal. What should a strong view answer?

options.text: Whether Monsanto was a good company
Whether Bayer paid any premium at all
Good for whom, at this price, and why
Whether the seed market was growing

questions.explain: A deal can be excellent for the sellers and hard for the buyer. A premium doesn't settle it: compare it with what the buyer gets.
questions.explain_at: Good for whom, at this price, because of what

questions.q: You'd buy Bayer's shares because the Supreme Court ruled for Monsanto. What's missing from that pitch?

options.text: The exact split of the court's vote
What the share price already assumes
A view on Bayer's drugs business

questions.explain: The ruling is public, so it's in the share price already. A pitch needs what's priced in, where you differ, a catalyst, and the risk against the reward.
questions.explain_at: That ruling is in the share price already

questions.q: At the end of the interview you're asked, "Do you have any questions for me?" What's the best approach?

options.text: Ask what you couldn't find online
Ask how your answers went today
Ask what the bonus usually is

questions.explain: Saying no sounds as if you've stopped being curious. Ask something the website can't answer, about a deal they worked on or someone you spoke to.
questions.explain_at: Ask something you couldn't find on the website
